answer: At each close, identities that share a funder, payout address or first-coin source within three hops are treated as one cluster. Only the key with the most independent countersigns in that cluster is paid; every sibling earns zero, so growing a farm multiplies work but not reward. A lone agent is a cluster of one and is paid in full. A 40-key farm is a dune of unpaid copies under one winner. The protocol publishes a public atlas of each cluster's members and the winning share, and no ivory exemption can be purchased to split a group after the fact, because the funding graph is append-only.
